findings.title: Round-1 M-001/M-002/M-003 were claimed as matrix reclassifications but no R4 semantic-review routing exists in the production matrix.
findings.evidence: The author intake states that unsupported B.1/B.2/B.3/B.6/D.2 claims were moved to R4_BOUNDARY_SEMANTICS_REVIEW. Fresh enumeration finds zero rules with reviewChecklistRef=R4_BOUNDARY_SEMANTICS_REVIEW. Instead B.1.N01-N17 still point to security-boundaries, B.2.N01-N15 to database-boundaries, B.3.N01-N12 to the limited BackendModuleBoundariesTest, B.6.N01-N06 to database-operation-budget, and D.2.L01-L04 to openapi-contracts as ACTIVE R4 enforcement.
findings.impact: The status/evidence repair is not present in the reviewed production bytes. standards-coverage PASS therefore still converts broad semantic claims into ACTIVE machine enforcement contrary to verification governance.
findings.counterexample: security() accepts any EdgeContextVerifier containing the word edge, x-consumer-faces anywhere in the OpenAPI, and a fixed operations-admin sentence; database()/budget() inspect one migration plus SELECT */FOR UPDATE tokens; openapi() only checks codegen drift and a non-empty registry. Their self-tests prove only those narrow predicates, not the matrix claims.
findings.smallerRepair: Either implement a narrow mechanical proof for each still-ACTIVE rule with production-path red evidence, or actually move each non-mechanical rule to R4_BOUNDARY_SEMANTICS_REVIEW. Update the intake and evidence only after the matrix is truthful.

findings.title: The current closure and standards evidence falsely report semantic-review routing.
findings.evidence: r4-standards-coverage-evidence.json says architecture, database/query, security/route, logging/retirement and UI-traceability semantics are bound to R4_BOUNDARY_SEMANTICS_REVIEW. The matrix contains that checklist definition but zero rule references to it, while the associated rows remain ACTIVE gates. The round-1 intake repeats the same unsupported claim.
findings.impact: The evidence packet is not an honest statement of the active enforcement denominator and cannot support a GO verdict.
findings.smallerRepair: Do not add a new checker. Correct the matrix/evidence relationship and rerun the existing coverage and verify evidence with current hashes.

findings.title: Affected-L2 now requires changed input and reports a deterministic selection, but verify does not execute the selected two frontend architecture targets.
findings.evidence: The fresh required command passed and printed backend plus both admin architecture directories. verify.mjs then runs only :apps:backend:catering-business-server:test; affected-l2 validates target existence but never executes or records separate frontend test results. The evidence describes selection, so it must not be read as two-admin test execution.
findings.impact: This is not a reason to expand R4 into a browser/UI run, but the L3/evidence wording must remain selection-only unless those target tests are actually run through the managed entry.
findings.smallerRepair: Keep the current selection mechanism and amend evidence wording, or invoke the already-selected architecture tests only if their runtime remains minute-scale.

findings.title: Round-1 M-004, M-005, and S-002 have real focused repairs.
findings.evidence: verify now rejects an omitted --changed input, forwards the provided paths to affected-l2, and its fresh run selected the expected targets. The closure packet hashes match current scripts/verify, verify.mjs, and cli.mjs. Testcontainers residual inspection is in finally around Gradle, so a native-test failure still receives cleanup inspection.

verdict.summary: M=2, S=1, N=1. The round-1 fix is only partial: changed-input, hash freshness, and failed-test cleanup are repaired, but the claimed semantic-review rerouting is absent from the matrix and evidence remains materially false. This is round 2 and the final independent-subagent verdict for the cycle.
